# Q-BOT by Q-Leap

> Q-BOT is a physical robot that automates two-factor authentication (2FA) — including LuxTrust hardware tokens — for software testing (Selenium, Cypress, Playwright, Appium, Robot Framework, CI/CD pipelines). It physically presses the 2FA device, reads the one-time code with a camera, and returns it over a REST API. Designed and manufactured by Q-Leap in Bertrange, Luxembourg.

Q-BOT solves a problem no software-only tool can: 2FA methods that require a physical action (a hardware token button, a phone notification) cannot be automated by a browser driver like Selenium. Q-BOT is a robot, not a script — it interacts with the real device the same way a human tester would, then exposes the resulting OTP code through an HTTP API that test scripts call directly.

Key facts:
- Subscription: €900/month, all inclusive (support, replacement, no long-term commitment).
- Hardware: Raspberry Pi 5, OLED display, Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/Gigabit Ethernet, 40×24×15 cm.
- Compatible with: LuxTrust (physical token and mobile), Google/Microsoft Authenticator, most smartphone-based 2FA.
- Compatible test frameworks: Selenium, Cypress, Playwright, Appium, Robot Framework, TestComplete, Jenkins, GitLab CI.
- Privacy: screenshots are deleted immediately after OTP extraction; no data retention; runs on the customer's local network.
- Company: Q-Leap, 10B rue des Mérovingiens, L-8070 Bertrange, Luxembourg. Contact: bot@q-leap.eu / +352 20 21 17.

Site available in French (default, root paths) and English (`/en/`).
